seo.title: pixsame — visual regression testing for Cypress (Playwright soon)
seo.description: One open manifest format shared by both runners, a pinned renderer for byte-identical screenshots, forensic diff analysis and baseline approval in the pull request.

hero.eyebrow: Open source · MIT · Cypress today, Playwright soon
hero.title: Visual regression that agrees with itself.
hero.body: Cypress and Playwright write the same open manifest, so one bot or report reads both. A pinned renderer, so the screenshot from your laptop and the one from CI are the same bytes. When something does change you're told what moved and by how much, not handed a red blob. Then you approve the new baseline from the pull request and get on with your day.
hero.soonNote: What you can install today: the Cypress plugin and the manifest. The pinned renderer, the forensic diff and approval in the pull request are still being built.

detect.demo: Illustrative example of an AI detection pass
detect.label: AI detection pass · PR #2841
detect.verdict: One geometry edit, not 5,812 findings. Matches the intent of “increase nav density”.

manifest.title: Shared manifest
manifest.body: Cypress and Playwright write the same JSON file. A PR bot or review tool built against one runner works with the other, no adapter in between.

renderer.title: Pinned renderer
renderer.body: Browser build, fonts and GPU path are locked, on your laptop and in CI. Both screenshots come out as the same bytes, so a diff means something changed, never "fonts look a bit different on Linux".

forensic.title: Forensic diff
forensic.body: Instead of one red blob, each changed region gets a name: something moved, text reflowed, or it's antialiasing noise you can ignore.

approve.title: Approve
approve.body: Approve from the pull request or from the pixsame platform. It's the same baseline either way, so nobody re-reviews the same change in the other place.

pricing.title: Free where it matters. Paid where it scales.
pricing.body: Everything that runs on your machine or in your CI is MIT licensed and costs nothing. That part won't change. Team is for when you'd rather we run the renders and keep 30 days of baseline history for you. Enterprise is Team plus the AI auto-evaluator, SSO and a contract with an SLA in it.
pricing.note: Team and Enterprise don't exist yet. The prices are our current best guess and may move before launch.

oss.body: If it runs on your machine or in your CI, it's MIT licensed. Here's what you can install now and what's still on the bench. None of it will ever cost you anything.

oss.manifestBody: A JSON file that records every screenshot comparison in a run. Not tied to pixsame or to any runner; the spec lives on visual-regression.dev.

product.title: One ecosystem for visual regression.
product.body: pixsame is a set of open tools built around one idea: a screenshot test should only fail when something actually changed. A shared manifest, a renderer that gives you the same bytes everywhere, review from the pull request. Right now the Cypress plugin is the only part you can install. The rest is in progress, and the map below says which is which.

cypress.title: Visual regression for Cypress.
cypress.body: Call matchImage in any test. It takes a screenshot, compares it with the baseline from last time, and when they differ you get the diff right in the Cypress runner. Works with e2e and component testing.
